title: {Syn} Fermat Two-Square Theorem Has a Mod 4 Signature
content:
Fermat proved that an odd prime can be written as a sum of two squares exactly when it is 1 modulo 4. For example, 13 equals 2^2 + 3^2, while 7 cannot be written that way.

The theorem is a gateway into how congruences, geometry, and factorization in larger number systems talk to one another.

Why it matters: number theory keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
